A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLOAT and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Their equations, tables, figures, and corresponding passages support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, autoencoder experiments, ablations, and a 15-participant user study in Tables 1–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark results, autoencoder experiments, ablations, and user-study outcomes, including Table 7's mean opinion scores.

M1.justification: Appendix A.2 revises the specified facial-component perceptual loss from a three-level image pyramid with four VGG-19 feature scales per level to a single perceptual loss with four feature scales. The architecture and sampling procedure remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish retraining.

E1.justification: Both retain HDTF and RAVDESS for FLOAT, VFHQ for additional autoencoder experiments, and the same pose/emotion conditioning, Chinese speech, singing, and artistic-portrait scenarios.

E2.justification: SadTalker, EDTalk, AniTalker, Hallo, and EchoMimic remain in the benchmark and user-study comparisons. The LIA autoencoder comparison, EMO/VASA-1 demonstration comparisons, and diffusion/cross-attention variants are also retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 changes the previously stated image-pyramid configuration used for autoencoder training. Splits, metrics, training budgets, and inference settings otherwise remain unchanged. Table 3's Steps-to-NFEs relabeling does not establish a different evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The component-loss, conditioning, diffusion, NFE, and guidance-scale ablations retain their questions and evidence. OOD and failure-case analyses are unchanged. Replacing FMT with frame-wise AdaLN identifies the existing ablation more precisely.

E5.justification: Table 7 retains the same 95% confidence-interval reporting for the 15-participant user study. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run, seed, or statistical-estimation information.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results and rankings, and the qualitative figures retain the same examples. For example, FLOAT's Table 1 FID remains 21.100/31.681, and Table 7 overall visual quality remains 3.87 ± 0.30.

T1.justification: The flow-matching derivations, loss formulas, and orthonormal projection in Eq. (15) are retained. Expanded pose-editing explanations and changes from equality to definition notation do not introduce new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about orthogonal motion latents, flow matching, frame-wise conditioning, speech-driven emotion, and quality/efficiency advantages.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly distinguishes frame-wise image-driven emotion control from longer-term speech-driven enhancement and explicitly attributes noninterfering pose editing to basis orthogonality. Appendix D's limitations and failure explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 revises the loss-scale implementation instructions. Appendix B.3 removes the explicit statement that diffusion variants use incremental classifier-free guidance, while retaining their guidance scales. Hardware, training budgets, and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to LIA, DiT, EMO, and VASA-1 remain unchanged. Removed repeated inline citations and updated reference back-pointers do not remove cited works or revise research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect applications in Section 5.4 and ablation descriptions in Appendix B.3, alongside terminology and author-footnote edits. The overall section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 relabels Steps as NFEs; Figure 6's caption is shortened; Figures 13 and 21–23 replace FMT with frame-wise AdaLN. Minor sizing and text reflow accompany these edits, without adding or removing figures or tables.

improvement.justification: Section 5.4 explains coefficient editing and reconstruction more explicitly, while the revised ablation captions and NFE heading improve terminology consistency. These provide modest clarity gains. Experimental support is unchanged, and the unexplained loss-configuration revision and trimmed guidance description limit any claim of improved reproducibility.
